event: The Exchange smells of burnt coffee and desperation as Callum weaves through the morning crowd.
He has come for four Echo Stones, the anchors the 80%-built Enhancement Construct still needs.
Echo Stones come from the Shardfield, Tier 2-3, where his constructs cannot survive.
A mineral vendor with a Vanguard tabard over one shoulder wants two hundred Gold each.
Eight hundred would breach his emergency buffer, and the price has doubled in two weeks.
"Supply's tight," the vendor shrugs; the Vanguard controls the Shardfield and the prices.
Three stalls down a young man pitches Iteration Tokens holding four thousand reps of a kill pattern.
The vendor walks off mid-pitch; the kid tells the empty air the yield curve is "a lot."
"Automation yield curve": Callum's own phrase, from page forty-seven of his notebook.
About nineteen, in a U of M hoodie under lopsided leather armor, hands full of amber tokens.
Callum walks over: "You know what Iteration Tokens are actually worth, don't you?"
He means in a compound loop, with an Enhancement Construct feeding back into the pattern.
The kid lights up: nobody in Detroit runs a closed compound loop, only flat parallel threads.
"Like running a factory with one conveyor belt," Callum says. "Who are you?"
"Jin. Jin Park. I'm a Summoner." Former U of M, computer science and applied math.
Jin reasons out Thread Spinner, then reads Callum's Idle Yield: over two, at Level 13.
"Your class is unique." Callum says nothing, and doesn't walk away. Jin offers coffee.
At a food stall on the Exchange's west edge, over something technically coffee, Jin talks.
Constructs are process threads, not soldiers, Jin says; the interesting part is the topology.
On a napkin he draws combat, gathering and processing, then adds an Enhancement node.
Output becomes the product, not the sum: the same diagram as Callum's notebook, page twelve.
Callum says the Enhancement Construct waits on Echo Stones at two hundred Gold each.
He shares his Gathering Construct's log with Jin, who reads it in twelve seconds.
The posted twelve-hour moss cycle is an average: the north regrows in 11h47m, the south 12h06m.
The timing costs about four percent; pre-sorting the Refinery's input would win back twelve.
A sorting function takes two or three lines, and Callum has headroom at Complexity 30.5.
A parallel path through the regeneration overlap zones would add eight percent more collection.
Three months walking the Overgrowth, six notebooks of data, and nothing to do with it, Jin says.
Callum's constructs can't reach past Tier 1; Jin has heard Mira partnered with him.
Even Mira can't farm the Shardfield sustainably alone, Jin says. His answer: his summons.
Chunk, a Level 14 earth elemental tank, has run six weeks; Zephyr, Level 13 wind, five.
His summons can kill there, but he has no collection or processing: a mine with no smelter.
Callum's factory would collect and refine, and the feedback would improve both their systems.
Jin's summons are effectively permanent idle loops: set and forget.
Chunk needs two weeks to hold the Shardfield alone, Zephyr three; faster with Callum collecting.
Pixel, a scout familiar, could map spawns ahead and pull singles, cutting multi-pulls sixty percent.
Nobody has done this, Jin says: Callum built a feedback system with scrap and a pipe wrench.
Mid-sentence about Echo Stones, the world flickers gold. Level up, 13 to 14.

changes.note: Level 13 to 14 while he sits in the food stall

event: He allocates at once: Intelligence to 53, Wisdom to 56, and one point of Vitality to 19.
The Vitality point is a concession to mortality, after Mira's evening lecture on dying.
"Did you just level up? While sitting in a food stall?" "My constructs are still running."
"That's the most beautiful thing I've ever heard. It's idle poetry," Jin says.
Jin wants to see the workshop, and has an idea: paired tokens as stand-in resonance nodes.
"Jin. Breathe." Jin laughs, startled: he talks a lot when excited, fair warning.
Nineteen, orphaned in the first wave, Jin is the first since the Emergence to speak his language.
"Finish your coffee. We'll walk back to the warehouse. I'll show you the topology."
They leave by the northern gate as the sky turns the colour of tarnished brass.
Jin covers summon AI, thread limits at INT 100, and Chunk learning to hide behind a rock.
Summon AI is grown by sustained deployment, Jin says; Callum's Compile Familiar may be the same.
Jin nearly walks into a lamp: three weeks running, Pip may be learning from Callum's patterns.
Pip blinks; Callum looks at it with new eyes. "We'll table that. Echo Stones first."
Near the warehouse, a prickle at the back of his neck: someone is watching.
An Iron Vanguard scout at a machine shop's corner, forty meters off, studies his Flux exhaust.
The scout notes the two of them, makes no move, and walks off; Jin, mid-sentence, never sees.
The Vanguard is watching his warehouse. Insufficient data; monitor. It feels like a shadow.
"You okay? You went quiet. Quieter." "I'm fine. Keep talking." "Bold instruction."
Inside the warehouse Jin turns a slow circle among the constructs, silent for four seconds.
"It's more beautiful than I imagined." He sits cross-legged on the floor and starts writing.
From the back, where she has been tending her sword, Mira calls: "Callum, who's the kid?"
"Jin Park. Summoner. He's going to help with the Shardfield problem."
Will he talk this much the entire time? "Almost certainly, yes," says Jin.
Mira looks him over, saber on her shoulder: "Three of us now. We're practically a guild."
"We're not a guild." "An optimized multi-class cooperative," Jin offers. "So a guild."
The sun drops behind the roofline; the chimney's Flux exhaust shimmers, visible for blocks.
Visible to anyone who is watching. And someone is.
